I investigated the use of std::ifstream::open(fileName) at lines 25 and 46. The function opens a file descriptor directly via the operating system’s open syscall and does not invoke a shell or interpret the filename as a command string. In POSIX and Windows, characters such as ';', '&', '|' are treated as literal characters in filenames and cannot trigger command execution. Therefore, even an attacker-supplied filename containing shell metacharacters cannot cause arbitrary OS command execution. The code merely reads the contents of the specified file.

No other part of the program constructs or executes a system command from the filename, so the CWE‑78 claim is unfounded.
